Consequent
A
consequent
is the second half of a hypothetical
proposition
. In the standard form of such a proposition, it is the part that follows "then". In an
implication
, if
P
implies
Q
, then
P
is called the
antecedent
and
Q
is called the
consequent
.
[
1
]
In some contexts, the consequent is called the
apodosis
.
[
2
]
Examples:
Q
{\displaystyle Q}
is the consequent of this hypothetical proposition.
Here, "
X
{\displaystyle X}
is an animal" is the consequent.
"They are alive" is the consequent.
The consequent in a hypothetical proposition is not necessarily a consequence of the antecedent.
"Fish speak Klingon" is the consequent here, but intuitively is not a consequence of (nor does it have anything to do with) the claim made in the antecedent that "monkeys are purple".
